changed_by.title: chore: bring in the setup and review changes of 22 November

adam.assumes: Page views on preview deployments, including every end-to-end test run against a preview, do not count toward the 50,000 Web Analytics events a month that the account's projects share on Hobby.
adam.if_wrong: Test runs use up the quota, and Vercel stops recording production visitors without telling anyone. Fix: render Analytics only when VERCEL_ENV is production.

changed_steps.step: Tell whether this job stopped at its time limit

lesson.summary: Run 45052415270 never reached what PR #648 changed: the time-limit step is skipped unless the job is cancelled, and this build finished normally, so there is nothing to change.
lesson.detail: PR #648 rewrote one step in `factory/workflows/implement.yml`, "Tell whether this job stopped at its time limit". It used to work out the minutes with GNU `date -d` and now uses jq's `fromdate` (decisions H632b), so the step also works on a Mac runner. The step only runs when the job is cancelled (`if: cancelled()`). In run 45052415270, Fred built issue #627 in 733 seconds, 22 turns and $0.89, and the run ended with conclusion `success`. The step was therefore skipped and its log is empty. The run neither confirms nor refutes the change. Adam's assumption on PR #648 is about Vercel Web Analytics counting preview page views. This run did not touch that, and no earlier lesson holds an assumption about it.

cost.amount: Nothing: the run finished its build ($0.89, 733 seconds) and the changed step never ran.

lesson.saves: Nothing: there was no fault to prevent.
